 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes — a phrase that hasn't been said in 24 years — host Pittsburgh today in their first game in daylight of the 2026 college football season.
 UM improved to 6-0 (4-0 in ACC) after a 43-35 double-overtime thriller against Florida State with Darian Mensah throwing three touchdowns but also his first interception with his new team. Malachi Toney remains the engine of the nation's No. 1 offense, but freshman running back Javian Mallory has overtaken Mark Fletcher Jr. as the team's leading rusher after a 108-yard, two-touchdown game last week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pitt (5-2, 2-2) enters on a two-game losing skid but fields the nation's top rushing defense, just ahead of Miami's. Senior Holden Geriner is expected to start over freshman Colin Dailey at quarterback with Mason Heintschel out with a torn ACL.

 Miami vs Pittsburgh history
 11:30 AM ET, October 24 2026, Dan Rorabaugh 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Miami holds a 30-12-1 advantage in the all-times series against Pitt, winning last year's meeting 38-7 in Pittsburgh. The Panthers won 42-16 the last time the teams played at Hard Rock Stadium to close the 2022 regular season. Here's a look at the most recent meetings (home team in bold:
 Nov. 29, 2025: Miami 38, Pitt 7 
 Nov. 26, 2022: Pitt 42, Miami 16 
 Oct. 30, 2021: Miami 38, Pitt 34 
 Oct. 17, 2020: Miami 31 , Pitt 19
 Oct. 26, 2019: Miami 16, Pitt 12 
 Who is starting for Pitt football at quarterback?
 11:15 AM ET, October 24 2026, Dan Rorabaugh 
 After Mason Heintschel tore his ACL on Oct. 2, senior Holden Geriner took over and started the followed week against North Carolina. Freshman Corey Dailey, a four-star recruit from Seguin, Texas, started last week against Boston College. CBS Sports reporter Mark Zenitz said Geriner would start against Miami, though Dailey also could see snaps. Here's a look at their stats this season:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Holden Geriner (4 games): 46 of 70 (65.7%) passing for 438 yards and 2 touchdowns with 2 interceptions; 11 carries for 22 yards
 Corey Dailey (2 games): 14 of 30 (46.7%) passing for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns with 2 interceptions; 4 carries for 9 yards

 Could Miami football leave ACC to go independent?
 10:55 AM ET, October 24 2026, Dan Rorabaugh 
 Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellinger published a lengthy article Thursday, Oct. 22, from an interview with Miami president Joe Echevarria, who stated plainly the school's aspirations to leave the ACC and join the Big Ten or SEC . The provisions limiting conference members in the current version of the Protect College Sports Act means the Hurricanes might instead become a football independent, which would be a return to their dynasty run in the 1980s until joining the Big East in 1991. "If we have to go independent, I like our chances because we are a national brand," Echevarria told Dellinger, at least as far as football goes.
